title.en: Joachim and Anna: The Childless Offering
title.zh: 約雅敬與亞拿：無子者的奉獻

region.zh: 耶路撒冷聖殿與牧人草場

texts.period: Gospel of the Birth of Mary, c. 150 CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: The Gospel of the Birth of Mary, chaps. 1-2 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

texts.license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: The pious couple Joachim and Anna, childless for twenty years, vow any child to the Lord; the high priest Issachar publicly rejects Joachim's offerings — 'cursed is every one who shall not beget a male in Israel.' Shamed, Joachim retires to the shepherds, where an angel of the Lord appears 'with a prodigious light', recalling Sarah and Rachel: 'when he shuts the womb of any person, he does it for this reason, that he may in a more wonderful manner again open it' — and promises a daughter to be called Mary.
summary.zh: 敬虔的約雅敬與亞拿無子二十年，起誓將孩子獻與主；大祭司以薩迦當眾拒其奉獻——「凡在以色列中不生男丁的，都是被咒詛的」。約雅敬羞愧退到牧人中間，主的使者帶著大光顯現，引撒拉與拉結為例：「神封閉人的胎，是為要以更奇妙的方式再開啟——使所生的不是情慾之果，而是神的恩賜」——並應許生女取名馬利亞。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal infancy-cycle text, formative for the Marian traditions (Nativity of Mary feast). Presented as legendary narrative, distinct from canonical scripture.

passages.text: Their lives were plain and right in the sight of the Lord, pious and faultless before men; for they divided all their substance into three parts; one of which they devoted to the temple and officers of the temple; another they distributed among strangers, and persons in poor circumstances; and the third they reserved for themselves and the uses of their own family. In this manner they lived for about twenty years chastely, in the favour of God, and the esteem of men, without any children.

Who, when he saw Joachim along with the rest of his neighbours, bringing his offerings, despised both him and his offerings, and asked him, Why he, who had no children, would presume to appear among those who had? Adding, that his offerings could never be acceptable to God; the Scripture having said, Cursed is every one who shall not beget a male in Israel. But Joachim being much confounded with the shame of such reproach, retired to the shepherds who were with the cattle in their pastures.

On a certain day when he was alone, the angel of the Lord stood by him with a prodigious light. And the angel who had appeared to him, endeavouring to compose him, said: Be not afraid, Joachim, nor troubled at the sight of me, for I am an angel of the Lord sent by him to you, that I might inform you that your prayers are heard, and your alms ascended in the sight of God. For God is the avenger of sin, and not of nature; and so when he shuts the womb of any person, he does it for this reason, that he may in a more wonderful manner again open it, and that which is born appear to be not the product of lust, but the gift of God.

title.en: Mary Danced on the Altar Steps
title.zh: 馬利亞在祭壇臺階上跳躍

texts.period: Protevangelion of James, c. 150 CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: The Protevangelion, chaps. 7-8 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

texts.license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: At three years old Mary is led to the temple by virgins bearing lamps 'that the child may not turn back again', received by the high priest — 'Mary, the Lord God hath magnified thy name to all generations' — placed on the third step of the altar, and there 'the Lord gave unto her grace, and she danced with her feet, and all the house of Israel loved her.' She is kept in the temple 'as a dove educated there', fed by the hand of an angel — the founding legend of the Presentation of Mary.
summary.zh: 三歲的馬利亞由持燈的童女引領入殿——「免得孩子回頭，心裏不願往主的殿去」——大祭司接納她並祝福：「馬利亞，主神已使你的名在萬代中得尊崇。」把她安置在祭壇第三級臺階上，「主賜她恩典，她便以足跳舞，以色列全家都愛她」。她如鴿子般住在殿中，「從天使手中得食」——馬利亞進殿節的傳說本源。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal; formative for the Presentation of Mary feast. Legendary narrative, distinct from canonical scripture.

passages.text: But the girl grew, and when she was two years old, Joachim said to Anna, Let us lead her to the temple of the Lord, that we may perform our vow. And Anna said, Let us wait the third year, lest she should be at a loss to know her father. And when the child was three years old, Joachim said, Let us invite the daughters of the Hebrews, who are undefiled, and let them take each a lamp, and let them be lighted, that the child may not turn back again, and her mind be set against the temple of the Lord. And they did thus till they ascended into the temple of the Lord.

And the high-priest received her, and blessed her, and said, Mary, the Lord God hath magnified thy name to all generations, and to the very end of time by thee will the Lord shew his redemption to the children of Israel. And he placed her upon the third step of the altar, and the Lord gave unto her grace, and she danced with her feet, and all the house of Israel loved her. And her parents went away filled with wonder, and praising God, because the girl did not return back to them.

But Mary continued in the temple as a dove educated there, and received her food from the hand of an angel. And when she was twelve years of age, the priests met in a council, and said, Behold, Mary is twelve years of age, what shall we do with her, for fear lest the holy place of the Lord our God should be defiled?

title.en: The Rods of the Widowers and Joseph's Dove
title.zh: 鰥夫之杖與約瑟杖上的鴿子

texts.period: Protevangelion of James, c. 150 CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: The Protevangelion, chap. 8 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

texts.license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: To keep the temple undefiled, the angel tells Zacharias to summon all the widowers of Judaea, 'every one of them bring his rod, and he by whom the Lord shall shew a sign shall be the husband of Mary.' The trumpet sounds, all assemble, and as the high priest prays over the rods, a dove comes forth from Joseph's rod and alights on his head. The old carpenter protests he has children and wants no wife; he is compelled, takes Mary home, and returns to his trade.
summary.zh: 為免聖所玷污，天使命撒迦利亞召集猶太全境的鰥夫，「各人拿自己的杖來，主藉誰顯出記號，誰就是馬利亞的丈夫」。吹角聚集後，大祭司拿杖禱告——「約瑟杖中飛出一隻鴿子，落在約瑟頭上」。老木匠連連推辭——「我有兒女，已經年老，再娶妻子豈合宜」——終被勸服，攜馬利亞回家，隨即重操建築舊業。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal betrothal legend; the sign-by-rod is a divination type noted as such.

passages.text: And behold the angel of the Lord came to him, and said, Zacharias, Zacharias, Go forth and call together all the widowers among the people, and let every one of them bring his rod, and he by whom the Lord shall shew a sign shall be the husband of Mary. And the criers went out through all Judaea, and the trumpet of the Lord sounded, and all the people ran and met together. And Joseph also throwing away his hatchet, went out to meet them; and when they were met, they went to the high-priest; taking every man his rod.

After the high-priest had received their rods, he went into the temple to pray; and when he had finished his prayer, he took the rods, and went forth and distributed them; and there was no miracle attending the last rod which Joseph took. But Joseph took the rod first of all the people... for a dove came out of the rod, and alighted upon his head.

title.en: Joseph's Dream and the Water of Ordeal

texts.period: Protevangelion of James, c. 150 CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: The Protevangelion, chaps. 10-11 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

texts.license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: Returning from building houses, Joseph finds his espoused wife grown big, and grieves in Adam's words — 'the serpent came and found Eve alone.' Mary answers with tears, 'I am innocent, and have known no man'; an angel settles the matter in a dream. Yet the scribe Annas drags both before the priest, and they drink the water of the Lord's ordeal, like the Sotah of Numbers — 'if any secret sin be in you, it will appear in your eyes' — and both go home unharmed, glorifying God.
summary.zh: 建屋歸來，約瑟見訂婚的妻已懷身孕，便照亞當的話哀哭——「蛇來時，夏娃獨自一人」。馬利亞流淚答「我是清白的，我從未認識男人」；天使在夢中化解此事。文士亞拿斯卻把二人拖到祭司面前，叫他們喝主的水行 ordeal（如民數記疑妻法）——「你們若隱瞞罪惡，必在你們眼中顯明」——二人毫無損傷回家，榮耀歸神。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal; the ordeal mirrors Numbers 5's Sotah rite; presented as legend.

passages.text: AND when her sixth month was come, Joseph returned from his building houses abroad, which was his trade, and entering into the house, found the Virgin grown big: then smiting upon his face, he said, With what face can I look up to the Lord my God? For I received her a Virgin out of the temple of the Lord my God, and have not preserved her such! Is not the history of Adam exactly accomplished in me? For in the very instant of his glory, the serpent came and found Eve alone, and seduced her. Just after the same manner it has happened to me.

But she, with a flood of tears, replied, I am innocent, and have known no man. Then said Joseph, How comes it to pass you are with child? Mary answered, As the Lord my God liveth, I know not by what means. Then Joseph was exceedingly afraid, and went away from her, considering what he should do with her; If I conceal her crime, I shall be found guilty by the law of the Lord; and if I discover her to the children of Israel, I fear, lest she being with child by an angel, I shall be found to betray the life of an innocent person. What therefore shall I do? I will privately dismiss her. Then the night was come upon him, when behold an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, and said, Be not afraid to take that young woman, for that which is within her is of the Holy Ghost.

And the priest said, Joseph, do that miracle which is required of you... And he took of the water of the ordeals and poured it upon the head of Joseph, and drank into his nostrils; and then he sent him out to walk about in a circuit... and returned without any harm, and glorified the God of Israel. And they did the same to Mary; and they both returned home without any harm, glorifying, and praising, and admiring the God of Israel.

texts.period: First Gospel of the Infancy of Jesus Christ, c. 6th-7th century CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: First Gospel of the Infancy of Jesus Christ, chap. 1 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

texts.license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: Framed as reports 'found in the book of Joseph the high-priest, called by some Caiphas', the infancy gospel opens with the infant Jesus speaking from the cradle and with the nativity moved to a cave: at sunset the midwife and Joseph enter, 'and behold, it was all filled with lights, greater than the light of lamps and candles, and greater than the light of the sun itself.' The old woman touches the infant at Mary's word and is healed of her infirmity; the cave 'seemed like a glorious temple' while angels and shepherds sing together.
summary.zh: 此福音託名「約瑟（該亞法）大祭司的書」：襁褓中的耶穌竟能說話。降生被置於洞穴：日落時分，接生婆與約瑟入洞——「看哪，洞裏充滿大光，勝過燈燭之光，也勝過太陽之光」。老婦照馬利亞的話伸手摸嬰孩，痼疾立愈；牧人歌唱之際，「那洞便如同榮耀的聖殿，天使與人的聲音一同讚美神」。

sensitivity.note: Late apocryphal infancy legend; basis of the cave-nativity tradition behind the Church of the Nativity's grotto.

passages.text: THE following accounts we found in the book of Joseph the high-priest, called by some Caiphas: He relates, that Jesus spake even when he was in the cradle, and said to his mother: Mary, I am Jesus the Son of God, that word, which thou didst bring forth according to the declaration of the angel Gabriel to thee, and my father hath sent me for the salvation of the world.

And when they came by the cave, Mary confessed to Joseph that her time of bringing forth was come, and she could not go on to the city, and said, Let us go into this cave. At that time the sun was very near going down. But Joseph hastened away, that he might fetch her a midwife. It was after sunset, when the old woman and Joseph with her reached the cave, and they both went into it. And behold, it was all filled with lights, greater than the light of lamps and candles, and greater than the light of the sun itself.

And as she was going forth, she said, From henceforth, all the days of my life, I will attend upon and be a servant of this infant. After this, when the shepherds came, and had made a fire, and they were exceedingly rejoicing, the heavenly host appeared to them, praising and adoring the supreme God. And as the shepherds were engaged in the same employment, the cave at that time seemed like a glorious temple, because both the tongues of angels and men united to adore and magnify God, on account of the birth of the Lord Christ.

title.en: Clay Birds That Fly and Cloths Dyed in the Furnace
title.zh: 會飛的泥雀與爐中染布

texts.period: First Gospel of the Infancy of Jesus Christ, c. 6th-7th century CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: First Gospel of the Infancy of Jesus Christ, chap. 15 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

texts.license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: At seven years old Jesus plays with boys his age, who make clay figures of asses, oxen, and birds; Jesus commands his figures to walk and his sparrows to fly — and they obey, even eating and drinking at his word. The alarmed fathers warn their children, 'he is a sorcerer; shun and avoid him.' Thence the dyer's shop of Salem: Jesus throws every cloth into the furnace, and draws them out dyed each to the colour its owner desired — 'and then he presently began to take the cloths out of the furnace.'
summary.zh: 七歲的耶穌與同齡孩童嬉戲，眾人以泥作驢、牛、雀鳥之形比賽；耶穌命己所造者行走、飛翔——皆聽命而行，甚至遵言而食。驚懼的父輩告誡孩子「他是行邪術的，務要遠避他」。他又入染匠沙倫的店中，把各家要染的布全數投入火爐——再取出時，每匹布都染上了各自想要的顏色。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal; the clay-birds episode has a parallel in the Quranic Infancy story (Surah 3:49) — noted as a shared motif.

passages.text: AND when the Lord Jesus was seven years of age, he was on a certain day with other boys his companions about the same age; who, when they were at play, made clay into several shapes, namely--asses, oxen, birds, and other figures; each boasting of his work, and endeavouring to exceed the rest. Then the Lord Jesus said to the boys, I will command these figures which I have made to walk. And immediately they moved, and when he commanded them to return, they returned. He had also made the figures of birds and sparrows, which, when he commanded to fly, did fly, and when he commanded to stand still, did stand still; and if he gave them meat and drink, they did eat and drink.

When at length the boys went away, and related these things to their parents, their fathers said to them, Take heed, children, for the future of his company, for he is a sorcerer; shun and avoid him, and from henceforth never play with him. On a certain day also, when the Lord Jesus was playing with the boys, he passed by a dyer's shop, whose name was Salem. And there were in his shop many pieces of cloth belonging to the people of that city, which they designed to dye of several colours. Then the Lord Jesus going into the dyer's shop, took all the cloths, and threw them into the furnace. And then he presently began to take the cloths out of the furnace, and they were all dyed of those same colours which the dyer desired.

title.en: Thecla at the Window of Iconium

texts.period: Acts of Paul and Thecla, c. 180 CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: Acts of Paul and Thecla, chaps. 9-10 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

texts.license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: The betrothed virgin Thecla sits at her window 'like a spider's web fastened to the window', three days without food, 'captivated by the discourses of Paul' in the house of Onesiphorus across the way — preaching one God and chastity. Her mother and her bridegroom Thamyris weep and plead in vain; the whole city is stirred, and Thamyris drags Paul before the governor, while Thecla's mother demands, 'Burn the lawless one! Burn her that are unwilling to marry, in the midst of the theatre, that all the women who have been taught by this man may also be afraid.'
summary.zh: 已許配人的處女特格拉在窗邊「如蛛網黏在窗上」，三日不食不飲，只為隔壁奧尼色弗家中保羅的講道著迷——宣講獨一真神與貞潔之道。母親與未婚夫他米利哀哭勸說皆無效，全城為之震動；他米利將保羅拖到方伯面前，其母則喊道：「燒死那不法者！把那不肯嫁人的燒死在戲院當中，好叫所有受這人教導的女人都懼怕。」

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal; the Thecla cycle was among the most beloved legends of the early church and remains part of Eastern Orthodox tradition.

passages.text: WHILE Paul was preaching this sermon in the church which was in the house of Onesiphorus, a certain virgin named Thecla (whose mother's name was Theoclia, and who was betrothed to a man named Thamyris) sat at a certain window in her house. From whence, by the advantage of a window in the house where Paul was, she both night and day heard Paul's sermons concerning God, concerning charity, concerning faith in Christ, and concerning prayer; nor would she depart from the window, till with exceeding joy she was subdued to the doctrines of faith.

But when she would not be prevailed upon to depart from the window, her mother sent to Thamyris, who came with the greatest pleasure, as hoping now, to marry her. Theoclia replied, Thamyris, I have something very strange to tell you; for Thecla, for the space of three days, will not move from the window, not so much as to eat or drink, but is so intent in hearing the artful and delusive discourses of a certain foreigner. For that man has disturbed the whole city of Iconium, and even your Thecla, among others. All the women and young men flock to him to receive his doctrine; who, besides all the rest, tells them that there is but one God, who alone is to be worshipped, and that we ought to live in chastity. Notwithstanding this, my daughter Thecla, like a spider's web fastened to the window, is captivated, by the discourses of Paul, and attends upon them with prodigious eagerness, and vast delight.

title.en: Thecla Among the Beasts: A Cloud of Fire
title.zh: 特格拉與猛獸：火雲護身

texts.period: Acts of Paul and Thecla, c. 180 CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: Acts of Paul and Thecla, chaps. 21-22 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

texts.license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: Condemned to the beasts in the theatre of Antioch, Thecla sees the pit of water and declares, 'Now it is a proper time for me to be baptized... In thy name, O my Lord Jesus Christ, I am this last day baptized' — and leaps in before the horrified crowd. Lightning and fire kill the seals; 'a cloud of fire surrounded Thecla; so that as the beasts could not come near her, so the people could not see her nakedness'; the women scatter perfumes till the beasts lie as if asleep, and the bulls' cords are burnt away as she stands 'as unconcerned as if she had not been bound.'
summary.zh: 特格拉被判喂獸，見場中有水坑便說：「現在正是我受洗的時候……主耶穌基督啊，我在你名裏今天受洗」——當眾縱身入水。閃電與火擊斃海豹；「火雲圍繞特格拉，猛獸不能近她，眾人也不能看見她的身體」；婦女們遍撒香膏使群獸如睡，綁牛的繩索被火燒斷——她「安然立於場中，若無其事」。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal; the self-baptism in the arena is the legend's signature scene and a famous image of women's apostolic authority.

passages.text: Then a she-bear ran fiercely towards her, but the she lion met the bear, and tore it in pieces. Again a he-lion, who had been wont to devour men, and which belonged to Alexander, ran towards her; but the she-lion encountered the he-lion, and they killed each other. Then the women were under a greater concern, because the she-lion, which had helped Thecla, was dead. Afterwards they brought out many other wild beasts; but Thecla stood with her hands stretched towards heaven, and prayed; and when she had done praying, she turned about, and saw a pit of water, and said, Now it is a proper time for me to be baptized. Accordingly she threw herself into the water, and said, In thy name, O my Lord Jesus Christ, I am this last day baptized.

But the fish (sea-calves) when they saw the lightning and fire, were killed, and swam dead upon the surface of the water, and a cloud of fire surrounded Thecla; so that as the beasts could not come near her, so the people could not see her nakedness. Yet they turned other wild beasts upon her; upon which they made a very mournful outcry; and some of them scattered spikenard, others cassia, others amomus... so that the quantity of ointment was large, in proportion to the number of people; and upon this all the beasts lay as though they had been fast asleep, and did not touch Thecla.

Then they put a cord round Thecla's waist, which bound also her feet, and with it tied her to the bulls, to whose privy-parts they applied red-hot irons, that so they being the more tormented, might more violently drag Thecla about, till they had killed her. The bulls accordingly tore about, making a most hideous noise; but the flame which was about Thecla, burnt off the cords which were fastened to the members of the bulls, and she stood in the middle of the stage, as unconcerned as if she had not been bound.

title.en: Go and Teach the Word of the Lord

region.zh: 安提阿至以哥念與西流基

texts.period: Acts of Paul and Thecla, c. 180 CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: Acts of Paul and Thecla, chap. 25 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

texts.license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: Freed at last, Thecla finds Paul in Myra — 'I have been baptized, O Paul; for he who assists you in preaching, has assisted me to baptize' — and reports all that befell her in Antioch. Then she speaks her commission and receives the apostle's blessing: 'I am going to Iconium. Paul replied to her: Go and teach the word of the Lord.' She returns to preach at Iconium and withdraws to Seleucia, where a rock opens to receive her — the legend behind the great Thecla shrine at Maaloula and Selucia.
summary.zh: 終於獲釋的特格拉在密拉尋見保羅——「保羅啊，我已受洗；那協助你講道的，也協助了我受洗」——並述說在安提阿的一切。隨後她宣明己志：「我要往以哥念去。」保羅答：「去把主的道傳開。」她重返以哥念傳道，退居西流基，岩石裂開接納了她——敘利亞馬魯拉與西流基大聖堂傳說的本源。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal; Thecla remains venerated (equal-to-the-apostles) in Eastern Orthodox and Maronite memory.

passages.text: Which when Thecla perceived, she said to him: I have been baptized, O Paul; for he who assists you in preaching, has assisted me to baptize. Then Paul took her, and led her to the house of Hermes; and Thecla related to Paul all that had befallen her in Antioch, insomuch that Paul exceedingly wondered, and all who heard were confirmed in the faith.

Then Thecla arose, and said to Paul, I am going to Iconium. Paul replied to her: Go and teach the word of the Lord. So Thecla went to Iconium. And when she came to the house of Onesiphorus, she fell down upon the floor where Paul had sat and preached, and, mixing tears with her prayers, she praised and glorified God: O Lord the God of this house, in which I was first enlightened by thee; O Jesus, son of the living God, who wast my helper before the governor, my helper in the fire, and my helper among the beasts; thou alone art God for ever and ever, Amen.

title.en: The King of Glory at the Gates of Hell

region.zh: 陰間黃銅之門（異象之境）

texts.period: Gospel of Nicodemus, c. 4th-5th century CE (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: The Gospel of Nicodemus (formerly the Acts of Pontius Pilate), chaps. 16-17 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

texts.license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: The descent into hell as Christian epic: a voice of thunder cries 'Lift up your gates, O ye princes... and the King of Glory shall come in'; David and Isaiah testify from among the dead; the prince of hell bars his brass gates 'with iron bars, and fight courageously, lest we be taken captives' — and the mighty Lord 'appeared in the form of a man, and enlightened those places which had ever before been in darkness. And broke asunder the fetters which before could not be broken.' The West's most quoted underworld scene, behind the Apostles' Creed's 'descended into hell' and the Paschal icons of Eastern Christianity.
summary.zh: 基督教史詩式的冥界下行：雷聲般呼喊「眾君侯啊，抬起你們的門……榮耀之王將要進來」；大衛與以賽亞在死者中作證；陰間君侯以鐵閂緊閃黃銅門「奮勇抵抗，免得我們被擄」——然而大能的主「以人的形像顯現，照亮了歷來的黑暗之地，掙斷了從前掙不斷的鎖鏈」。西方使徒信經「降在陰間」與東方復活節聖像的文本根源。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal but theologically formative; the 'harrowing of hell' is one of the tradition's great underworld narratives, central to Paschal liturgy in the East.

passages.text: AND while Satan and the Prince of hell were discoursing thus to each other, on a sudden there was a voice as of thunder, and the rushing of winds, saying, Lift up your gates, O ye princes; and be ye lift up, O everlasting gates, and the King of Glory shall come in. When the prince of hell heard this, he said to Satan, Depart from me, and begone out of my habitations; if thou art a powerful warrior, fight with the King of Glory. And the prince said to his impious officers, Shut the brass gates of cruelty, and make them fast with iron bars, and fight courageously, lest we be taken captives.

But when all the company of the saints heard this they spake with a loud voice of anger to the prince of hell, Open thy gates, that the King of Glory may come in. And the divine prophet David cried out, saying, Did not I, when on earth, truly prophesy and say... For he hath broken the gates of brass, and cut the bars of iron in sunder. After this, another prophet, namely, holy Isaiah, spake in like manner to all the saints, The dead men shall live, and they shall rise again who are in their graves. And I said in another place, O grave, where is thy victory? O death, where is thy sting?

Then was there a great voice, as of the sound of thunder, saying, Lift up your gates, O princes; and be ye lifted up, ye gates of hell, and the King of Glory will enter in. The prince of hell perceiving the same voice repeated, cried out, as though he had been ignorant, Who is that King of Glory? David replied to the prince of hell... the Lord strong and powerful, the Lord mighty in battle: he is the King of Glory, and he is the Lord in heaven and in earth. And now, thou filthy and stinking prince of hell, open thy gates, that the King of Glory may enter in; for he is the Lord of heaven and earth. While David was saying this, the mighty Lord appeared in the form of a man, and enlightened those places which had ever before been in darkness. And broke asunder the fetters which before could not be broken.

title.en: Come to Me, All Ye My Saints: Adam Led Up
title.zh: 凡我聖徒都到我這裏來：亞當被領上來

texts.period: Gospel of Nicodemus, c. 4th-5th century CE (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: The Gospel of Nicodemus, chap. 19 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

texts.license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: The second Adam reverses the first: 'Jesus stretched forth his hand, and said, Come to me, all ye my saints, who were created in my image, who were condemned by the tree of the forbidden fruit... Live now by the wood of my cross.' The Lord lays hold of Adam's hand, Adam sings the psalm 'O Lord thou hast brought up my soul from the grave', and 'taking hold of Adam by his right hand, he ascended from hell, and all the saints of God followed him' — David singing a new song behind. The classic image of the harrowing, Christ's hand in Adam's wrist, painted from the Easter icon westward.
summary.zh: 末後的亞當逆轉首先的亞當：「耶穌伸手說，凡我的聖徒，按我形像受造、因那棵禁果樹被定罪的，都到我這裏來……如今靠我十字架的木頭得以存活。」主握住亞當的手；亞當唱詩「主啊，你曾把我的靈魂從陰間救上來」；主「握住亞當右手，從陰間升上去，神的眾聖徒跟隨其後」——大衛在後高唱新歌。這「拉住亞當手腕」的經典畫面，自東方復活節聖像傳遍西方。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal; the Adam-led-up image is the tradition's emblem of reversal of the fall (recapitulation).

passages.text: THEN Jesus stretched forth his hand, and said, Come to me, all ye my saints, who were created in my image, who were condemned by the tree of the forbidden fruit, and by the devil and death; Live now by the wood of my cross; the devil, the prince of this world, is overcome, and death is conquered. Then presently all the saints were joined together under the hand of the most high God; and the Lord Jesus laid hold on Adam's hand, and said to him, Peace be to thee, and all thy righteous posterity, which is mine.

Then Adam, casting himself at the feet of Jesus, addressed himself to him with tears, in humble language, and a loud voice, saying, I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me. O Lord my God, I cried unto thee, and thou hast healed me. O Lord thou hast brought up my soul from the grave; thou hast kept me alive, that I should not go down to the pit.

O Lord, as thou hast put the ensigns of thy glory in heaven, and hast set up the sign of thy redemption, even thy cross on earth; so, Lord, set the sign of the victory of thy cross in hell, that death may have dominion no longer. Then the Lord stretching forth his hand, made the sign of the cross upon Adam, and upon all his saints. And taking hold of Adam by his right hand, he ascended from hell, and all the saints of God followed him. Then the royal prophet, David, boldly cried, and said, O sing unto the Lord a new song, for he hath done marvellous things; his right hand and his holy arm have gotten him the victory.

title.en: The Letter of Abgar of Edessa
title.zh: 伊得撒王阿布加爾書信

region.zh: 伊得撒城，奧斯若恩王國

texts.period: Correspondence tradition, c. 4th-5th century CE (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: The Epistles of Jesus Christ and Abgarus King of Edessa, chaps. 1-2 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

texts.license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: The sick king Abgar writes to Jesus: 'either that you are God himself descended from heaven... or the Son of God... My city is indeed small, but neat, and large enough for us both.' Jesus answers — 'Abgarus, you are happy, forasmuch as you have believed on me, whom you have not seen' — promising after his ascension to send a disciple who will cure him. Eusebius cites the letters; Edessa became the tradition's first royal Christian city, and the portrait-promise of the exchange seeded the Image of Edessa legends.
summary.zh: 患病的阿布加爾王寫信給耶穌：「或者你自己就是從天上降下的神……或者你是神的兒子……我的城雖小，卻整潔，足以容你與我。」耶穌回信道：「阿布加爾，你因未見而信，便是有福的」——應許升天後差門徒醫治。優西比烏引此書信；伊得撒遂為傳統首座基督徒王城，畫像之諾亦播下「伊得撒聖像」傳說的種子。

sensitivity.note: Legendary correspondence cited by Eusebius (Hist. Eccl. I.13); formative for Edessa's Christian royal legend.

passages.text: ABGARUS, king of Edessa, to Jesus the good Saviour, who appears at Jerusalem, greeting. I have been informed concerning you and your cures, which are performed without the use of medicines and herbs. For it is reported, that you cause the blind to see, the lame to walk, do both cleanse lepers, and cast out unclean spirits and devils, and restore them to health who have been long diseased; and raiseth up the dead. All which when I heard, I was persuaded of one of these two, namely, either that you are God himself descended from heaven; who do these things, or the Son of God. On this account therefore I have written to you, earnestly to desire you would take the trouble of a journey hither, and cure a disease which I am under. My city is indeed small, but neat, and large enough for us both.

ABGARUS, you are happy, forasmuch as you have believed on me, whom you have not seen. For it is written concerning me, that those who have seen me should not believe on me, that they who have not seen might believe and live. As to that part of your letter, which relates to my giving you a visit, I must inform you, that I must fulfil all the ends of my mission in this country, and after that be received up again to him who sent me. But after my ascension I will send one of my disciples, who will cure your disease, and give life to you, and all that are with you.

title.en: Hermas Rebuked by the Heavenly Lady

region.en: Vision-place by the river Tyber, Rome
region.zh: 羅馬，台伯河邊異象之境

texts.period: Shepherd of Hermas, Visions I-II, c. 90-140 CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: The Shepherd of Hermas, Visions 1-2 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

texts.license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: Nearly canonical in some early lists, Hermas the former slave sees the woman he once coveted 'saluting me from heaven' with an accusation: 'the desire of naughtiness has risen up in thy heart... as for those who think wickedly in their hearts, they take to themselves death and captivity.' A later vision shows the church as an aged lady 'because she was created first of all', her chair of white wool, and a book of revelations she bids him copy — the Shepherd's visions became Rome's beloved manual of penitence.
summary.zh: 在某些早期正典目錄中近於正典的黑馬書：曾為奴的黑馬見昔日暗戀的婦人「從天上向我問安」並責備他：「淫念已在你心中興起……心中思想惡事的人，是自取死亡與捆鎖。」後續異象中，教會顯為「因先被造而顯老」的婦人，坐白羊毛之椅，授書命他抄錄——這位「牧者」的異象成為羅馬教會悔改生活的最愛讀本。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal-but-beloved (Muratorian fragment debate); presented as early Christian vision literature.

passages.text: HE who had bred me up sold a certain young maid at Rome; whom when I saw many years after, I remembered her, and began to love her as a sister. It happened some time afterwards, that I saw her washing in the river Tyber; and I reached out my hand unto her, and brought her out of the river. And when I saw her I thought with myself, saying, How happy should I be if I had such a wife, both for beauty and manners. This I thought with myself; nor did I think any thing more.

And as I was praying, the heaven was opened, and I saw the woman which I had coveted, saluting me from heaven, and saying, Hermas, hail! and I looking upon her, answered, Lady, what dost thou do here? She answered me, I am taken up hither to accuse thee of sin before the Lord. God who dwelleth in heaven, and hath made all things out of nothing, and hath multiplied them for his holy church's sake, is angry with thee because thou hast sinned against me.

Then she, smiling upon me, said: the desire of naughtiness has risen up in thy heart. Does it not seem to thee to be an ill thing for a righteous man to have an evil desire rise up in his heart. It is indeed a sin, and that a very great sin, to such a one; for a righteous man thinketh that which is righteous. And whilst he does so, and walketh uprightly, he shall have the Lord in heaven favourable unto him in all his business. But as for those who think wickedly in their hearts, they take to themselves death and captivity.
